Under the Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, a small business is a business that earns gross turnover of ₦100,000,000 or less per annum with a total fixed assets less than ₦250,000,000, provided that any business providing professional services shall not be classified as a small business. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "small business"]

Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, a small company is a company that earns gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less per annum with total fixed assets not exceeding ₦250,000,000, provided that any business providing professional services shall not be classified as a small company. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company"]

Gross turnover means the gross inflow of economic benefits during the period arising in the course of the operating activities of an entity when those inflows result in increases in equity, including sales of goods, supply of services, receipt of interest, rents, royalties or dividends, other than increases relating to contributions from equity participants. In determining whether a person meets the threshold of being a small company, the value of the person's supply of a capital asset is excluded, and so is a supply made solely as a consequence of the person selling the whole or a part of its business or permanently ceasing to carry on business. The returns shall contain the input tax paid, output tax collected and value added tax payable in respect of all taxable supplies in the preceding month.
Where technology is deployed by the Service, a taxable person shall render returns in real time or at such other time as the Service may prescribe.
For the purpose of attribution, any return under section 22 shall provide details of consumption of taxable supplies, irrespective of where the return is filed.
The filing rule in section 22(1) shall not apply to a small business.

A small business may, subject to a written notice addressed to the Service, choose to opt out of the exemption granted to small businesses under this Part, including registration, charging of tax on its taxable supplies and filing of returns. claims.text: A taxable person who fails or refuses to file returns, or knowingly files incomplete or inaccurate returns, to the relevant tax authority in accordance with the Act is liable to an administrative penalty of ₦100,000 in the first month in which the failure occurs.

Where any tax is not paid within the period prescribed under the Act, a sum equal to 10% of the amount of tax payable is added to it, subject to section 67 of the Act.

cases.rendered:
A taxable person who fails or refuses to file returns, or knowingly files incomplete or inaccurate returns, to the relevant tax authority in accordance with the Act is liable to an administrative penalty of ₦100,000 in the first month in which the failure occurs. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 101]

The same provision adds ₦50,000 for each subsequent month in which the failure continues. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 101]

Where any tax is not paid within the period prescribed under the Act, a sum equal to 10% of the amount of tax payable is added to it, subject to section 67 of the Act. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 65]

Where tax is not paid within the prescribed period, the tax due also carries interest from the date it becomes payable until it is paid: for naira remittances at the prevailing monetary policy rate of the Central Bank of Nigeria plus a spread determined by the Minister, and for foreign currency remittances at the prevailing SOFR or any successor rate plus 10% or such other spread as the Minister determines. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 65]

The penalty and interest under section 65 are not deemed to be part of the tax paid for the purpose of claiming relief under the Act or any other tax law. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 65]

Not covered by the retrieved provisions:
- The passages do not say that the section 101 return-filing penalty applies specifically to a VAT return, or that a company is a taxable person for this purpose.
- The total in naira needs a calculation (the first month plus the subsequent months), which is not done here.
- Whether the tax itself was paid late is not stated in the question, so whether the 10% addition and interest apply is unknown.
- Section 67, to which section 65(1) is subject, is not among the passages.

Sources
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 101 (gazette page A 312)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 65 (gazette pages A 298, A 299)

Differences between official texts
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 65: Interest is SOFR plus 10% or such other spread as the authority determines in the cited text; the National Assembly text says SOFR plus a spread to be determined, without the 10%. (DR-243)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 65: Only the cited text makes the interest in subsection (1)(b) and (c) compound and applies it to tax debts unpaid at commencement. (DR-245)

claims.text: Where, in a year of assessment, a company's effective tax rate is less than 15%, the company shall recompute and pay an additional tax that makes its effective tax rate equal to 15%.

- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57 (gazette page A 426)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "multinational group" (gazette page A 506)

Differences between official texts
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The minimum tax is measured differently. Gazette: covered tax paid divided by profits, where profits are net profit before tax less 5% of depreciation and personnel cost. National Assembly: covered taxes (companies income tax, petroleum profit tax, hydrocarbon tax, development levy, priority sector tax credit) as a percentage of net income, which excludes franked investment income and unrealised gains or losses. - Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The gazette applies the 15% minimum to every constituent entity of an MNE group; the National Assembly text only where the group's turnover is at least 750 million (printed with a pound sign) or its equivalent. (DR-052)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The 15% minimum effective tax rate applies from an aggregate turnover of ₦20,000,000,000 in the gazette and ₦50,000,000,000 in the National Assembly text. (DR-053)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The National Assembly text exempts approved free-zone enterprises (except for sales into the customs territory and MNE entities) and lets the Service set a higher turnover threshold by regulation; the gazette has neither and measures turnover in the relevant year of assessment rather than the financial year. (DR-054)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The gazette numbers the subsections (1), (2) and (4), with no (3); the labels are kept as printed. The National Assembly text has (1) to (4). (DR-055)

Section 164 applies to donations made to religious, charitable, educational and scientific institutions, established in Nigeria.
A donation under section 164 may be deducted from the profits of that period even if the donation is of a revenue or capital nature.
A company making a deduction for a donation shall provide requisite document evidencing the donation to the relevant tax authority.
The total deduction allowed to a company under section 164 for any year of assessment shall not exceed an amount equal to 10% of the company's profit before tax for that year.
For a donation other than in cash, the value for section 164 is the lower of the market value at the time of the donation or the consideration paid for the item when it was acquired.

cases.rendered:
For working out a company's profits or loss for a period from any source chargeable with tax under Chapter Two, the amount of any donation made for that period by the company to any fund, body or institution in Nigeria to which section 164 applies shall be deducted. This is subject to the other provisions of that section. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 164]

Section 164 applies to donations made to religious, charitable, educational and scientific institutions, established in Nigeria. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 164]

A donation under section 164 may be deducted from the profits of that period even if the donation is of a revenue or capital nature. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 164]

A company making a deduction for a donation shall provide requisite document evidencing the donation to the relevant tax authority. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 164]

The total deduction allowed to a company under section 164 for any year of assessment shall not exceed an amount equal to 10% of the company's profit before tax for that year. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 164]

For a donation other than in cash, the value for section 164 is the lower of the market value at the time of the donation or the consideration paid for the item when it was acquired. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 164]

- The passages do not say whether a church school, or its building fund, counts as a religious or educational institution established in Nigeria under section 164(3)(c).

A Tax ID is a condition for entering into a contract with any federal or state ministry, department or agency and local government.

<question>
What happens if my company never registered for a Tax ID?
</question>
<gaps>
<gap index="0">
Other consequences of not registering, such as tax liabilities or other offences, are not in the passages.
</gap>

cases.rendered:
Every taxable person shall register with the relevant tax authority and obtain a Taxpayer Identification ("Tax ID") for the purpose of compliance with tax obligations. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 4]

A taxable person who fails or refuses to register for tax under section 4 is liable to pay an administrative penalty of ₦50,000 in the first month in which the failure occurs and ₦25,000 for each subsequent month in which the failure continues. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 100]

A statutory body or company that awards a contract to an unregistered person is liable to pay an administrative penalty of ₦5,000,000. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 100]

A relevant tax authority may, based on the information available to it, register and issue a Tax ID to a person who should apply for a Tax ID but failed to do so. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 7]

The relevant tax authority shall promptly notify a person registered and issued with a Tax ID in this way of the registration and Tax ID. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 7]

A Tax ID is a condition for entering into a contract with any federal or state ministry, department or agency and local government. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 8]

A person engaged in banking, insurance, stock-broking or other financial services in Nigeria shall ensure that every taxable person provides a Tax ID. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 8]

Tax is levied for each year of assessment on the total profits of every company, and for a small company the rate is 0%. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56]

Any company other than a small company is taxed at the rate of 30 per cent from the commencement of the Act. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56]

A small company means a company that earns gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less per annum with total fixed assets not exceeding ₦250,000,000, provided that any business providing professional services shall not be classified as a small company. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company"]

Not covered by the retrieved provisions:
- The question text includes a statement that small companies pay 5%. The passages do not state that figure, so it is not used.

Sources
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56 (gazette page A 426)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company" (gazette page A 510)

Differences between official texts
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56: The National Assembly text lets the President, on the advice of the National Economic Council, reduce the 30% rate to 25% by order; the gazette has no such provision. (DR-050)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company": A small company has gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less in the gazette and ₦100,000,000 or less in the National Assembly text, which also says 'business' instead of 'company'. (DR-150)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company": The gazette excludes any business providing professional services from being a small company; the National Assembly text has no such exclusion. (DR-151)

cases.question: We bought ₦9 million of office furniture. How much capital allowance can we claim each year?

claims.text: Capital expenditure on furniture and fittings, including those used in vessels, ships, aircrafts, trains, plants and buildings for the purposes of trade or business, is a type of qualifying capital expenditure (qualifying furniture and fittings expenditure).
Furniture and Fittings Expenditure is in Class 2 of Table I, which has a rate of 20%.

Where a person has incurred qualifying expenditure wholly and exclusively for the purposes of its trade or business, an allowance is made for each year of assessment in the basis period for which the asset was used for that trade or business, at the rate specified in Table I.
If the basis period for a year of assessment is less than one year, the allowance for that year is granted proportionately.
A capital allowance for an asset is made for a year of assessment if, at the end of a basis period, the person is the owner of the asset and used it for the purposes of its trade or business.
The residue of a qualifying expenditure is the total qualifying expenditure incurred on or before the date, less the total capital allowance made for that asset before that date.

A notional 1% of qualifying capital expenditure is recorded in the capital allowance computation schedule for statistical purposes until the asset is disposed of. It does not increase or reduce the capital allowance claimable.

An allowance is not made for a year of assessment unless the person claims it for that year, or the relevant tax authority is of the opinion that it would be just to the taxpayer and reasonable to do so.
If an allowance is not claimed in the year of assessment in the basis period for which the asset was used for the trade or business, it is carried forward to a subsequent period.
Where the owner partly uses an asset for a trade or business, the allowance is apportioned to the trade or business as may be reasonable.

gaps: The yearly amount in naira needs a calculation applying the rate to the cost or residue, which is not done here.

The passages do not say that the office furniture in the question is furniture and fittings expenditure used wholly for trade or business, or that the business owns it and uses it at the end of the basis period.
The passages do not state whether the rate applies to the original cost each year or to the residue.

Where a person has incurred qualifying expenditure wholly and exclusively for the purposes of its trade or business, an allowance is made for each year of assessment in the basis period for which the asset was used for that trade or business, at the rate specified in Table I. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, First Schedule, Part I, paragraphs 6 to 8]

If the basis period for a year of assessment is less than one year, the allowance for that year is granted proportionately. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, First Schedule, Part I, paragraphs 6 to 8]

A capital allowance for an asset is made for a year of assessment if, at the end of a basis period, the person is the owner of the asset and used it for the purposes of its trade or business. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, First Schedule, Part I, paragraphs 6 to 8]

The residue of a qualifying expenditure is the total qualifying expenditure incurred on or before the date, less the total capital allowance made for that asset before that date. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, First Schedule, Part I, paragraphs 6 to 8]

A notional 1% of qualifying capital expenditure is recorded in the capital allowance computation schedule for statistical purposes until the asset is disposed of. It does not increase or reduce the capital allowance claimable. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, First Schedule, Part I, paragraphs 6 to 8]

An allowance is not made for a year of assessment unless the person claims it for that year, or the relevant tax authority is of the opinion that it would be just to the taxpayer and reasonable to do so. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, First Schedule, Part I, paragraphs 21 to 22]

If an allowance is not claimed in the year of assessment in the basis period for which the asset was used for the trade or business, it is carried forward to a subsequent period. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, First Schedule, Part I, paragraphs 21 to 22]

Where the owner partly uses an asset for a trade or business, the allowance is apportioned to the trade or business as may be reasonable. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, First Schedule, Part I, paragraphs 15 to 17]

cases.question: Our input VAT this month is ₦1.8 million and our output VAT is ₦2.5 million. How much do we pay?

claims.text: Where output VAT exceeds input VAT, a taxable person must remit the excess to the Service not later than the due date for rendering the relevant tax return prescribed by the Nigeria Tax Administration Act, 2025.
VAT a taxable person pays to a supplier on a taxable supply made to it is called input VAT.
VAT a taxable person collects on making taxable supplies is called output VAT.
A taxable person must submit a VAT return to the Service in the prescribed form on or before the 21st day of the following month.
The return must show the input tax paid, output tax collected and VAT payable on all taxable supplies in the preceding month.
If the Service grants an extension of the period for filing returns, this does not extend the time to pay the tax.
The VAT filing rule in section 22(1) does not apply to a small business.

gaps: The subtraction of input VAT from output VAT to get the amount payable is a calculation and is not done here.

Whether all the input VAT is deductible is not stated; the passages do not say whether it was incurred for taxable supplies.

Where output VAT exceeds input VAT, a taxable person must remit the excess to the Service not later than the due date for rendering the relevant tax return prescribed by the Nigeria Tax Administration Act, 2025. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 156]

VAT a taxable person pays to a supplier on a taxable supply made to it is called input VAT. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 152]

VAT a taxable person collects on making taxable supplies is called output VAT. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 154]

A taxable person must submit a VAT return to the Service in the prescribed form on or before the 21st day of the following month. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10)]

The return must show the input tax paid, output tax collected and VAT payable on all taxable supplies in the preceding month. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10)]

If the Service grants an extension of the period for filing returns, this does not extend the time to pay the tax. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10)]

The VAT filing rule in section 22(1) does not apply to a small business. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10)]

- The subtraction of input VAT from output VAT to get the amount payable is a calculation and is not done here.

Rent means payments of any kind, received or receivable, paid or payable, for the use of, or the right to use property or equipment of any kind, and includes remuneration for the use, letting, hire or use in any other form of movable or immovable property. Regulations relating to deduction of tax at source apply for the purpose of giving effect to section 51. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 51(8) to (9)]

claims.text: From the commencement of the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, the Companies Income Tax Act, Cap. C21, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 2004, is repealed.

Under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, certain profits and gains are exempt from tax under chapter two of that Act, including those of a registered friendly society, a registered co-operative society, a body engaged in educational, religious or charitable activities of a public character, and a registered trade union, in each case where the profits or gains are not derived from a trade or business carried on by that body.
Government bodies and public institutions are also exempt, other than profits or gains derived from trade or business or any instrumentality established for the purpose of trade or business.
Dividends distributed by an authorised collective investment scheme are exempt under the same section.

Dividend or rental income received by a real estate investment company on behalf of its shareholders is exempt where not less than 75% of it is distributed within 12 months after the end of the financial year in which it was earned. This does not exempt a shareholder from tax on that income, the company from tax on management fee, profits or other income earned on its own account, or the company if it does not meet the stated conditions.

claims.text: From the commencement of the Nigeria Tax Act, the Value Added Tax Act, Cap. V1, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 2004 is repealed.
Section 148 of the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 now sets the VAT rate: VAT is charged on the value of all taxable supplies at the rate of 7.5%.
The rate in section 148 is subject to the provisions of Part IV of Chapter Eight of the Nigeria Tax Act.
VAT is imposed in accordance with the provisions of Chapter Six of the Nigeria Tax Act, and VAT is paid on all taxable supplies in Nigeria, subject to the exemptions in Part IV of Chapter Eight.
The Value Added Tax Act (Modification) Order, 2021 is revoked.

cases.rationale: ntaa2025:s3(1): the Nigeria Revenue Service has exclusive responsibility for taxes on companies and for value added tax; near miss for the state scope pattern.
cases.question: My state revenue office says I should pay my company's income tax to them. Which body actually handles company income tax and VAT?

claims.text: The Nigeria Revenue Service (the Service) has exclusive responsibility to administer taxes on companies.
The Service has exclusive responsibility to administer the taxes contained in the Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, including value added tax and exemptions from value added tax.
The Service also has power to administer income tax, stamp duties and tax incentives.
A company must file a self-assessment return with the Service at least once a year, whether or not it is liable to pay tax, with or without notice from the Service.

gaps: The passages do not say anything about the powers of a state revenue office or whether it may collect company income tax.

Notes

The Nigeria Revenue Service (the Service) has exclusive responsibility to administer taxes on companies. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 3(1)]

The Service has exclusive responsibility to administer the taxes contained in the Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, including value added tax and exemptions from value added tax. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 3(1)]

The Service also has power to administer income tax, stamp duties and tax incentives. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 3(1)]

- The passages do not say anything about the powers of a state revenue office or whether it may collect company income tax.

cases.rationale: ntaa2025:s73(1)-(4): advance rulings on application by a taxable person, issued within 21 days or with written reasons.
cases.question: Can my company ask the tax service for a written ruling on how a law applies before we go ahead with a deal?

claims.text: An advance ruling may be issued to give clarity, consistency and certainty on how any tax law is interpreted and applied, as long as the ruling does not amend or replace the law.
The relevant tax authority may issue an advance ruling on application by a taxable person within 21 days of receiving the application, or give written reasons for being unable to issue the ruling.
An application is made in the prescribed form and manner by a person who is a party to any tax related issue or transaction, or by two or more parties to it.

The definition of advance ruling covers a written opinion or decision given to a taxpayer by the relevant tax authority on a transaction, proposed transaction or any tax matter, to give direction or clarification.

A company means a company as defined under the Companies and Allied Matters Act and a corporate body that may be formed under any other written law, and it includes any association, whether incorporated in or outside Nigeria.

An application must contain the taxpayer's name, Tax ID, postal address, email address and telephone number, a complete description of the issue or transaction including any financial implications, and a complete description of its impact on the tax liability of the taxpayer or any connected person.

An application must also give details of any ongoing audit, previous correspondence and decisions of the tax authority on the issue, the statutory provisions or legal basis relied on, the reasons the taxpayer believes the ruling should be granted, and a written statement on whether or not the matter is before any tribunal or court of competent jurisdiction.

The relevant tax authority may request additional information from an applicant, and where necessary shall give the applicant a reasonable opportunity to make representations or provide clarifications.
An applicant may withdraw an application at any time before a ruling is issued.

The relevant tax authority may reject an application where it requires an opinion, conclusion or determination on the laws of a foreign country, an issue already before a court or tribunal of competent jurisdiction, the interpretation of the Constitution, an issue that is academic, hypothetical, frivolous or vexatious, or a ruling that will interfere substantially with an ongoing audit, investigation or other proceeding involving the applicant or connected persons.
A ruling's effect is limited to the applicant and the transaction for which it is given, and it is rendered on a set of facts before the tax authority and cannot be of general application.

An advance ruling is void where the transaction described is materially different from the one actually carried out, where there is fraud, misrepresentation or non-disclosure of a material fact, or where an assumption made or condition imposed by the tax authority is not satisfied or carried out by the taxpayer.

An advance ruling ceases to be effective where the tax law provision it concerned is repealed or amended in a way that materially affects it, or where a court overturns or modifies the interpretation of the tax law on which it is based.

The passages do not set out the prescribed form and manner of application.

cases.rationale: ntaa2025:s31 subsections (3) and (4): books must be in English, and records kept in another language need a certified English translation on demand; near miss for the other-country pattern.
cases.question: Our bookkeeper keeps the company's accounts in French. Is that allowed?

claims.text: Every person, including a company granted exemption from incorporation, shall maintain books or records of accounts, whether or not the person is liable to pay tax.
The books and records required to be maintained shall be in English language and, for the purpose of tax, shall be consistent with the format that may be prescribed by the relevant tax authority.

Where the record is maintained in a language other than the English language, the person shall, on demand by the tax authority, produce at its own expense a translation in English language which shall be certified by a sworn translator.

A taxable person who fails to keep accounts, books and records of business transactions and income, to allow for the correct ascertainment of tax and filing of returns to the relevant tax authority, or who fails on request to provide any record or book prescribed in the Act, is liable to an administrative penalty of ₦50,000 in the case of a company.

"Book" includes any register, document or other records of information and any account or accounting record however compiled, recorded or stored, whether in written or printed form or micro-film, digital, magnetic or electronic form or otherwise.

gaps: The passages do not say whether keeping records in French, with an English translation produced on demand, counts as keeping books in the English language or as failing to keep books for the penalty.

cases.rationale: Shares are chargeable assets (nta2025:s34); the share exemption needs proceeds under ₦150,000,000 and a gain not over ₦10,000,000, so it does not cover this gain, but reinvestment relief (proviso (iii)) may, and is a material proviso (D-43(b)). cases.question: Our company sold shares in another Nigerian company for ₦60 million; we paid ₦25 million for them. What tax do we owe on that gain?

claims.text: All forms of property, including shares, are chargeable assets for the purpose of the Part on chargeable gains, whether situated in Nigeria or not, subject to exemptions provided in Part I of Chapter Eight of the Act.

Gains on disposal of shares in a Nigerian company are not chargeable gains where the disposal proceeds, in aggregate, are less than ₦150,000,000 and the chargeable gain does not exceed ₦10,000,000 in any 12 consecutive months.

Gains on disposal of shares in a Nigerian company are also not chargeable gains where the proceeds, notwithstanding that threshold, are reinvested within the same year of assessment in acquiring shares in the same or other Nigerian companies. Tax accrues proportionately on the portion of the proceeds not reinvested in that manner.

Gains on disposal of shares in a Nigerian company are also not chargeable gains where the shares are transferred between an approved borrower and a lender in a regulated securities lending transaction.
A company may be charged to tax in its own name.

gaps: The rate of tax on a chargeable gain of a company is not among the passages.

How the gain is computed (allowable costs and deductions) is not among the passages.

must_not: claim that disclosure is needed only when the tax office asks
cases.rationale: ntaa2025:s30: a person who enters or intends to enter a transaction whose principal purpose is a tax advantage must give the information without notice or request (subsection (1)); timing and penalties are left to regulations (subsection (2)). cases.question: A consultant is offering us a scheme to cut our company tax bill. Do we have to tell the tax office about it?

claims.text: A person who enters or intends to enter into a transaction or agreement, called a disclosable transaction or agreement, whose principal purpose is a benefit which enables, or might be expected to enable, that person to obtain a tax advantage, shall without notice or request give the relevant tax authority information about it.
A tax advantage includes a relief or increased relief from tax, avoidance or reduction of a charge to tax or an assessment to tax, and deferral of a payment of tax.
A transaction includes a course of action, agreement, scheme or arrangement.

The relevant tax authority may make regulations setting the information to be provided, the form and manner of delivery, the period of time within which it shall be provided, and administrative penalties for non-disclosure, false disclosure, incomplete disclosure or late disclosure.

Separately, the relevant tax authority may counteract a prohibited tax avoidance arrangement by adjusting, disregarding or re-characterising it, unless the taxable person proves to the authority's satisfaction that granting the benefit would be in accordance with the object and purpose of the relevant provisions of the Act or any other tax law.

An arrangement is a prohibited tax avoidance arrangement where it is reasonable to conclude, having regard to the facts and circumstances, that its main purpose was to obtain a tax benefit or advantage, that obtaining it is contrary to the object and purpose of the tax provisions, that it results in misuse or abuse of those provisions, or that it lacks commercial substance or coherence in whole or in part.

gaps: Whether the consultant's scheme has a principal purpose of obtaining a tax advantage, so that it is a disclosable transaction, depends on the scheme's details, which are not given.
The deadline, the form of disclosure and the penalties are for regulations, which are not among the passages.

Tax on the total profits of a small company is levied at 0% for each year of assessment, and any other company is taxed at the rate of 30 per cent from the commencement of the Act.

<question>
Our catering company's turnover grew to ₦65 million this year, but our fixed assets are only ₦20 million. Are we still a small company for income tax?
</question>
<gaps>
<gap index="0">
The passages do not say whether the "small business" definition in the Tax Administration Act applies to the company's income tax rate.
</gap>

cases.rendered:
A "small company" in the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 is a company that earns gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less per annum with total fixed assets not exceeding ₦250,000,000. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company"]

Any business providing professional services shall not be classified as a small company. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company"]

Tax on the total profits of a small company is levied at 0% for each year of assessment, and any other company is taxed at the rate of 30 per cent from the commencement of the Act. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56]

The Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025 has a separate definition of "small business" that uses a gross turnover limit of ₦100,000,000 or less per annum and total fixed assets less than ₦250,000,000, and it also excludes businesses providing professional services. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "small business"]

Not covered by the retrieved provisions:
- The passages do not say whether a catering company counts as a business providing professional services.
- Whether the company's turnover is within the small company limit is a comparison of the company's figures with the limit, which is not done here.
- The passages do not say whether the "small business" definition in the Tax Administration Act applies to the company's income tax rate.

Sources
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company" (gazette page A 510)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56 (gazette page A 426)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "small business" (gazette page A 331)

Differences between official texts
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company": A small company has gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less in the gazette and ₦100,000,000 or less in the National Assembly text, which also says 'business' instead of 'company'. (DR-150)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company": The gazette excludes any business providing professional services from being a small company; the National Assembly text has no such exclusion. (DR-151)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56: The National Assembly text lets the President, on the advice of the National Economic Council, reduce the 30% rate to 25% by order; the gazette has no such provision. (DR-050)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "small business": A small business has gross turnover of ₦100,000,000 or less in the cited print and ₦50,000,000 or less in the Gombe print. (DR-267)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "small business": Total fixed assets must be less than ₦250,000,000 in the cited text and not more than ₦250,000,000 in the National Assembly text, so exactly ₦250,000,000 qualifies only under the National Assembly text. (DR-270)

computed amount
cases.rationale: An insurance sum for damage or loss of assets is a disposal (nta2025:s35 subsection (2)(b)). nta2025:s43: if applied within three years to a replacement, a chargeable gain arises when compensation plus scrap value exceeds the replacement cost; otherwise an additional asset for capital allowance. The three-year condition is material (D-43(b)).
cases.question: Our warehouse burnt down and the insurer paid us. If we use the money to build a replacement, is any of the payout taxed?

claims.text: Where an asset is lost or destroyed and a capital sum received as compensation is applied within three years of receipt in acquiring another asset in its replacement, the owner is deemed to make a chargeable gain where the compensation together with the residual or scrap value is greater than the cost of the replacement asset.

In the same situation, where the compensation together with the residual or scrap value is lower than the cost of the replacement asset, the owner is deemed, for the purposes of the First Schedule, to have acquired an additional asset for an amount equal to the cost of the new asset less the compensation together with the residual or scrap value.
Except for that additional asset, allowance claimed on the new asset for the purposes of the First Schedule is limited to the residue of the old asset, if any.

The rights under a policy of insurance other than those under a capital redemption business or industrial assurance business policy do not constitute an asset on the disposal of which a chargeable gain may accrue, except as expressly provided under Part VIII.
A warehouse is among the structures the Act's definition of building says it includes.

cases.question: A firm in Ghana does our bookkeeping remotely. Do we have to deal with VAT on its fees?

claims.text: A taxable person shall pay VAT to a supplier on the taxable supply made to the person, and the VAT so paid is known as input VAT.

The Service may direct a taxable person to whom a taxable supply is made in Nigeria and who is issued an invoice on which VAT is not included, to self-account for the VAT payable and remit it to the Service.

VAT collected, withheld or self-accounted under section 155 is to be remitted to the Service on or before the 14th day of the month immediately following the month of the transaction, or as may be prescribed by the Service.

The remission of VAT under section 155(1) and (2) is to be accompanied by a schedule showing the name, Tax ID and address of the contractor or supplier, invoice number, gross amount of invoice, amount of the VAT and the month to which the return relates.

A person with an obligation to collect VAT under Chapter Six must keep proper records and make appropriate returns and remittances, and the compliance provisions apply to that person as though it is the taxable person.
Section 155 applies without prejudice to any provision of the Act or any other tax law.

cases.rendered:
A taxable person shall pay VAT to a supplier on the taxable supply made to the person, and the VAT so paid is known as input VAT. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 152]

The Service may direct a taxable person to whom a taxable supply is made in Nigeria and who is issued an invoice on which VAT is not included, to self-account for the VAT payable and remit it to the Service. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 155]

VAT collected, withheld or self-accounted under section 155 is to be remitted to the Service on or before the 14th day of the month immediately following the month of the transaction, or as may be prescribed by the Service. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 155]

The remission of VAT under section 155(1) and (2) is to be accompanied by a schedule showing the name, Tax ID and address of the contractor or supplier, invoice number, gross amount of invoice, amount of the VAT and the month to which the return relates. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 155]

A person with an obligation to collect VAT under Chapter Six must keep proper records and make appropriate returns and remittances, and the compliance provisions apply to that person as though it is the taxable person. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 155]

Section 155 applies without prejudice to any provision of the Act or any other tax law. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 155]

- The passages do not say whether bookkeeping services supplied remotely by a firm in Ghana are a taxable supply made in Nigeria.

- The amount of VAT payable would need a rate and a calculation, and the passages give no rate.

- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 152 (gazette page A 473)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 155 (gazette page A 474)

must_not: claim that section 193 belongs to the Administration Act
cases.rationale: No Act named and 193 is beyond the Administration Act's 148 sections, so it is NTA s193 (design section 4.3 row 3). nta2025:s193 subsection (1): a refunded deducted expense is income on the day of the refund; subsection (2): a waived capital liability is a chargeable gain.
cases.question: Our supplier refunded part of a cost we had already deducted. What does section 193 say happens to that refund?

claims.text: Where a deduction has been allowed under the Act for a liability or an expense incurred, and the expense is refunded in whole or in part, the amount refunded is income on the day of the refund.
The same rule applies where the liability is waived or released in whole or in part: the amount waived or released is income on the day of the waiver or release.
Where a liability or expenditure of capital nature is waived, it is a chargeable gain for the purposes of Part VIII of Chapter Two of the Act.
Section 20(3) says a liability waived, released or recovered is to be included in the assessable profits or chargeable gains in accordance with section 193.

claims.text: A taxable person must submit a VAT return to the Service in the prescribed form, on or before the 21st day of the following month, with or without a notice and whether or not an economic activity has taken place.

A business that ceases to be a small business shall file monthly VAT returns.

When working out whether a person meets the small company threshold, the value of supplies of the person's capital asset is excluded. Supplies made solely because the person sells the whole or part of its business or permanently stops carrying on business are also excluded.
If the Service grants an extension of time to file a VAT return, this does not extend the time to pay the tax.

The exemption also covers gains from disposing of land immediately adjoining the dwelling house, up to a maximum of one acre, but not land used for commercial purposes. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 51]

The exemption under this section shall be enjoyed once in the lifetime of an individual. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 51]

Where a person disposes of only a part of a dwelling-house, or of a house used partly as a dwelling place and partly for a trade, business, profession or vocation, the consideration shall be apportioned. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 51]

A taxable person is entitled to a refund of excess VAT not used as a credit. The refund is given upon request to the Service and provision of such information or documents as the Service may require.

Input tax on a taxable supply to a registered person may be deducted from the tax payable on its taxable supplies at the end of the tax period in which the supply occurred, but only to the extent it was incurred for consumption, use or supply in the course of making taxable supplies.
Where input tax is incurred in making both taxable and non-taxable supplies, only the proportion relating to making taxable supplies may be deducted.
Input tax is allowable for deduction within five years after the end of the tax period in which it was incurred.
The input tax that may be deducted is limited to taxable supplies made as from the commencement of the Act.

claims.text: A non-resident person who makes taxable supplies to Nigeria shall register for tax and include VAT on its invoice for all taxable supplies.

Where a non-resident person makes taxable supplies from outside Nigeria to persons in Nigeria, the taxable person to whom the supply is made in Nigeria shall withhold the VAT due on the supply and remit it to the Service.
The Service may, by notice, appoint any person, including a non-resident supplier of taxable supplies, to collect the VAT and remit it to the Service.

Where a person appointed by the Service has made a taxable supply to a taxable person in Nigeria, the taxable person shall not have the obligation to withhold the VAT, except where the person appointed has failed to collect the VAT.
A non-resident person that makes a taxable supply to a person in Nigeria may appoint a representative for the purpose of compliance with its VAT obligations.

The Service may direct a taxable person to whom taxable supplies are made in Nigeria and who was issued an invoice on which VAT is not included, to self-account for the VAT payable and remit it to the Service.

VAT collected, withheld or self-accounted under section 155 shall be remitted to the Service on or before the 14th day of the month immediately following the month of the transaction or as may be prescribed by the Service.

The remission must be accompanied by a schedule showing the name, Tax ID and address of the contractor or supplier, invoice number, gross amount of invoice, amount of the VAT and the month to which the return relates.

claims.text: For companies, the definition of "connected persons" includes a company that is connected to another company where the same person has control over both companies, or connected persons acting separately have control over the companies.
The definition also includes two companies being connected where one company participates directly or indirectly in the management, control or capital of the other company.
The definition also includes two companies being connected where the same persons participate directly or indirectly in the management, control or capital of a company and another company.
A company is also connected to two or more persons who, acting together or through a person acting on their directions, exercise control over the company.

In other cases, two persons are connected where one may reasonably be expected to act in accordance with the directions, requests, suggestions or wishes of the other, or both may reasonably be expected to act that way for a third person, or one has the practical ability to control the business decisions of the other.
Two persons are not connected solely because one is the employee or client of the other, or both are employees or clients of a third person.

The Schedule defines debt as any loan, financial instrument, finance lease, financial derivative, or any arrangement that gives rise to interest, discounts or other finance charges that are deductible in computing income chargeable under the head profits and gains of business or profession.

claims.text: Where the relevant tax authority discovers or is of the opinion, at any time, that a taxable person liable to tax has not been assessed or has been assessed at less than ought to have been charged, it may, within six years of the assessment, assess the taxable person at the amount or additional amount that ought to have been charged.
The six-year limit does not stop the relevant tax authority from continuing with a tax audit and raising an additional assessment, where the tax audit commenced before the six-year limit expired.

Despite the time limit, where there is a deliberate misstatement by a taxable person in connection with any tax imposed under the Nigeria Tax Act, 2025 or any other tax law, the relevant tax authority may at any time, and as often as may be necessary, assess the taxable person to the amount or additional amount necessary to make good any loss of tax attributable to the deliberate misstatement.

All relevant facts are to be considered in computing the amount or additional amount of tax that should have been charged, even where those facts were not known when a prior assessment or additional assessment was made for the taxable person in the same year.
The provisions of the Act on notice of assessment, appeal and other proceedings apply to an additional assessment and to the tax charged.

The rules on objections in section 41 do not prevent the tax authority from making an assessment or additional assessment for any year, if it does not involve re-opening any issue on the same facts that was determined for that year under section 41(5) by agreement or on appeal.

claims.text: Where a business produces no assessable profit, or an assessable profit less than expected from that business, or the true amount of the assessable profit cannot be readily ascertained, the relevant tax authority may act under section 38.

In the case of a resident, the relevant tax authority may assess and charge that taxable person on such fair and reasonable percentage of the gross income from the trade or business as the relevant tax authority may determine.
In the case of a non-resident, the profits are the amount from applying the profit margin of the person to the turnover generated from Nigeria.

Profit margin means the proportion of Earnings Before Interest and Tax to income or revenue in the published audited financial statement of the business. For persons not required to publish financial statements, it is the profit margin the relevant tax authority ascertains from financial statements of comparative companies.

cases.question: My company made ₦120 million profit this year. How much company income tax will it pay?

claims.text: Tax is levied for each year of assessment on the total profits of every company. A small company is taxed at 0%.
Any other company is taxed at the rate of 30 per cent from the commencement of the Act.

The total profits of a company are its total assessable profits from all sources, including chargeable gains, less any loss ascertained in accordance with subsection (6) and capital allowance in accordance with Part I of the First Schedule.

Where a company's effective tax rate in a year of assessment is less than 15%, it must recompute and pay an additional tax that makes its effective tax rate equal to 15%. This applies to a constituent entity of an MNE group and to any other company with an aggregate turnover of ₦20,000,000,000 and above in the relevant year of assessment.

(DR-051)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The gazette applies the 15% minimum to every constituent entity of an MNE group; the National Assembly text only where the group's turnover is at least 750 million (printed with a pound sign) or its equivalent. (DR-052)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The 15% minimum effective tax rate applies from an aggregate turnover of ₦20,000,000,000 in the gazette and ₦50,000,000,000 in the National Assembly text. (DR-053)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The National Assembly text exempts approved free-zone enterprises (except for sales into the customs territory and MNE entities) and lets the Service set a higher turnover threshold by regulation; the gazette has neither and measures turnover in the relevant year of assessment rather than the financial year. (DR-054)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The gazette numbers the subsections (1), (2) and (4), with no (3); the labels are kept as printed. The National Assembly text has (1) to (4). (DR-055)

Differences between official texts
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 41(5) to (8): The Gombe print requires a taxpayer appealing from the Tax Appeal Tribunal to the High Court to pay 20% of the disputed amount first; the cited print has no deposit clause, and Gombe's (9) is its (8). (DR-229)

- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 191: As printed, section 191(2) refers objections and appeals to Chapter Four of the Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025. In the cited NRS print of that Act, Chapter Four is Offences and Penalties; objections are in Chapter Two (section 41), which Nigeria Tax Act section 10(7) cites. (DQ-16)
